subject: Unexpected mid-cycle bulk ingestion overage and VAT line item
messages:
From: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@acme-analytics.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, billing@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-12T09:18:00-05:00
Subject: Question on January invoice: mid-cycle spike and VAT

Hi Rafael / Redwood billing team,

We opened the January invoice (INV-20260131) and see a large overage line for token consumption (approx +1.2M tokens) that we don't recognize. Our engineering team hasn't run any production job that would create that volume, and the embedded line also shows VAT applied even though ACME Analytics is an EU-registered business with a valid VAT ID (we supplied it at signup).

Can you provide an itemized activity log for Jan 29-31 (UTC) and confirm whether that consumption was billed as standard or zero-rated/reverse-charge for VAT? We'd like to place payment on hold until we get a breakdown — is that acceptable?

Attached: acme_usage_snapshot_20260211.csv (small sample from our dashboard), invoice_20260131.pdf

Thanks,
Elena Petrova
Finance Manager, ACME Analytics
Elena.Petrova@acme-analytics.com
+44 20 7123 9981
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-12T10:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Question on January invoice: mid-cycle spike and VAT

Hi Elena — thanks for flagging this and for the sample. Sorry for the hassle.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- I'll open a metering export request with finance (Ben cc'd) and ask for per-minute logs for Jan 29-31 UTC.
- Monica (CS) will coordinate with your engineering contact to confirm whether any ingestion jobs could have retried/duplicated.
- We'll pause collection on INV-20260131 for 10 business days while we investigate; if the investigation takes longer we'll extend the hold and let you know.

If we verify the consumption is duplicate/reprocessing we will: provide a corrective credit for the duplicate tokens, and re-issue the invoice with corrected VAT treatment (reverse-charge) if appropriate.

Can you also provide the VAT ID you have on file and the contact who can share the ingest job ids? A presigned logs link is fine if you prefer to upload samples.

I'll keep you updated by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 1122
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-12T10:12:00-05:00
Subject: Fwd: ACME invoice question — suspected duplicate bulk ingest (internal)

Team — forwarding ACME's note. Quick context: ACME spotted ~1.2M tokens in a short window (Jan 29-31). They claim no corresponding job; they also say VAT should be reverse-charged.

Ben — can you run a metering export for ACME (acct: ACME-4112) covering 2026-01-29 00:00:00 UTC through 2026-01-31 23:59:59 UTC with request_id, model, token_count, route, and raw_request_id fields? We need per-request granularity to spot duplicates or retry storms. Please mark as high priority.

Marissa — if we confirm this was an internal duplication (e.g., API client replays) what is our standard credit policy for mid-cycle duplicate ingestion? Also confirm VAT handling for EU B2B reverse-charge and whether finance can reissue a corrected invoice.

Monica — please connect with ACME eng and ask for any job ids / manifests — they said they'll upload sample logs.

Thanks — Rafael

Hi Rafael — thanks for the quick reply.

VAT ID: EU123456789
ACME engineering has pulled a short manifest and found one workflow that appears to have reprocessed a 3GB dataset twice due to an orchestrator retry on Jan 30 03:12 UTC. We've attached the manifest with the duplicated job id and timestamps. It looks like two identical streams hit your API within a few seconds.

Attached: duplicate_job_manifest.csv

For the VAT: ACME is VAT-registered (EU123456789) and we expect reverse-charge/no VAT on the invoice; the current invoice shows VAT at 20% which inflates the amount.

Please let us know target date for a corrected invoice and provisional credit. We can provide engineering contact if you need further traces.

Best,
Elena
Finance Manager, ACME Analytics
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-16T17:22:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Question on January invoice: mid-cycle spike and VAT — resolution and next steps

Hi Elena — quick update and confirmation of next steps. Thanks for the manifest, that was helpful.

Findings:
- Ben's metering export shows two near-identical request streams for Jan 30 03:11:58–03:12:07 UTC totaling ~1.18M tokens. The request_id pattern and identical payload sizes indicate a retry storm from the orchestrator.
- We agree this appears to be duplicate processing rather than legitimate unique workload.

Agreed remediation:
1) Redwood will apply a provisional credit equal to the duplicate consumption (1,180,352 tokens) at the standard per-token rate; credit will appear on your account and offset INV-20260131.
2) Finance (Marissa cc'd) will re-issue INV-20260131 with corrected VAT treatment (reverse-charge, zero VAT) and a new invoice id: INV-20260131-R1. Expect the reissued PDF within 3 business days.
3) We will hold collection on the outstanding balance for 30 days while the reissued invoice propagates through your AP system.

Action items and owners:
- Ben Carter: finalize metering export and post the supporting CSV to the Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_link) — DONE.
- Marissa Cole: reissue invoice with reverse-charge and confirm tax commentary for ACME's AP team.
- Monica Patel: continue to be the customer touchpoint for any engineering questions; cc me on follow-ups.

I've opened a HubSpot ticket for tracking: https://hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-ACME-4112 (Ticket #11287). Please reply if anything is missing.

Thanks again for the patience — we'll confirm when the corrected invoice is issued.

Best regards,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
